sections.history: Uraiyur, remembered in old Tamil as Kozhi, was a capital of the early Cholas long before Thanjavur, and today lies within the city of Tiruchirappalli, a short way from Srirangam across the Kaveri. Its Vishnu temple, Thirukkozhi, is popularly called Nachiyar Koil, for here the Goddess Kamalavalli holds the place of honour. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Chola Nadu, sung in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham by Kulasekhara Alvar, the Chera king-saint devoted to Ranganatha, and by Thirumangai Alvar. Uraiyur is also revered as the birthplace of Thiruppan Alvar. The present temple is believed to go back to the Medieval Cholas, with later gifts from the Pandyas, the Vijayanagara kings and the Madurai Nayaks; it is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department.
sections.architecture: A five-tiered gateway tower leads into the temple, whose halls are known for richly carved pillars and broad mandapams. In the sanctum, beneath the Kalyana Vimanam, Azhagiya Manavalan stands facing north in his wedding form, and Kamalavalli Nachiyar shares the shrine with him — unusually, she has no separate sannidhi and is always seen together with the Lord. The temple tank, known as the Surya Pushkarini or Kalyana Theertham, has on its northern side a shrine to Thiruppan Alvar, honouring the saint born in this town.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of Kamalavalli, daughter of the Chola king Nanda Chola, who gave her heart to the Lord of Srirangam. In one telling she kept a long penance, and Vishnu came to Uraiyur as a radiant bridegroom to wed her — and so here he is Azhagiya Manavalan, the Beautiful Bridegroom, standing in the form of a groom. Because the Goddess is honoured as a daughter of the Chola house who became Ranganatha's bride, Uraiyur and Srirangam are bound together, and the bond is renewed each year in a wedding festival.
sections.festivals: The chariot festival in Chittirai (March–April) is the temple's great occasion, drawing the town onto its streets. On Panguni Pooram the festival image of Ranganatha is brought from Srirangam for the Kalyana Utsavam, the sacred wedding with Kamalavalli. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the days of the Alvars, Thiruppan Alvar above all, are kept with devotion.
sections.experience: A short ride from Srirangam, Uraiyur rewards the pilgrim who completes the visit to Ranganatha by coming to his bride's home. The mood is domestic and gentle — the Goddess at the heart of worship, the Lord beside her as a bridegroom — and the shrine of Thiruppan Alvar by the tank recalls the low-born singer who, tradition holds, was carried into the sanctum at Srirangam.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Chittirai chariot festival, Panguni Pooram and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Uraiyur lies within Tiruchirappalli, a few kilometres from the Chathiram bus stand and Tiruchirappalli Junction, and a short drive across the Kaveri from Srirangam; Tiruchirappalli International Airport is the nearest airport.
